standard_prerequisites.name: A finite morphism is proper, hence closed, and the inverse image of a closed nowhere dense subset under an open morphism is nowhere dense
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives closedness of the image and lets the nowhere density be transported along the open morphisms appearing in the auxiliary diagram.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nowhere density is local on the target, and a finite union of closed nowhere dense subsets is closed and nowhere dense
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to an affine base and assembles the final case from finitely many closed pieces.

standard_prerequisites.name: An open inverse image of a closed subset is closed, and the image of a closed nowhere dense subset under a closed immersion stays closed and nowhere dense
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the auxiliary diagram to be replaced by the situation where the source is a finite union of closed pieces mapping isomorphically to the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: The auxiliary diagram for a finite morphism over an affine base, with a finite locally free morphism to the target and to the source, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the open morphisms along which the problem is invariant.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite locally free morphism is flat, and a flat morphism locally of finite presentation is open, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the morphisms of the auxiliary diagram are open.

core_obligations: Closedness and reduction to an affine base: the image is closed because a finite morphism is proper, and since the trace of a nowhere dense closed subset on the preimage of an affine open is nowhere dense there, the local nature of nowhere density reduces the claim to an affine target (proof lines 12506-12513).

Auxiliary diagram: choose the finite locally free diagram for the finite morphism, note that its vertical morphisms are open, that the inverse image of the nowhere dense subset is nowhere dense, and that it suffices to prove nowhere density after pulling back along the surjective open morphism to the base; the image under the closed immersion stays nowhere dense, leaving the case where the source is a finite union of closed pieces each mapping isomorphically to the base (proof lines 12515-12535).

Easy case of the reduced situation: if for each piece the trace of the subset is nowhere dense in that piece, then its image is nowhere dense in the base because the piece maps isomorphically onto it, and the image of the whole subset is a finite union of such, hence nowhere dense (proof lines 12537-12548).

Contradiction in the remaining case: suppose some trace contains a nonempty open subset; intersecting successively with the other pieces splits the index set into those meeting that open subset and those disjoint from it while keeping an open subset of the first piece inside the given subset; its image is open in the base because the first piece maps isomorphically, and the displayed decomposition of the preimage of that image exhibits the open subset as open in the source, contradicting nowhere density (proof lines 12549-12570).
proof_roadmap: Get closedness and reduce to an affine base by locality of nowhere density (proof lines 12506-12513).

Use the finite locally free diagram to pass to the case of a finite union of closed pieces each mapping isomorphically to the base, dispose of the case where all traces are nowhere dense, and rule out the opposite case by exhibiting an open subset of the source contained in the subset (proof lines 12515-12570).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the image of a closed nowhere dense subset under a finite morphism is closed and nowhere dense (statement lines 12499-12504). The counted proof is a reduction chain of moderate length: after closedness and a reduction to an affine base by locality of nowhere density, it uses the auxiliary finite locally free diagram to replace the situation by one where the source is a finite union of closed pieces mapping isomorphically onto the base, handles the case where all traces are nowhere dense by taking a finite union, and rules out the remaining case by a careful argument that produces an open subset of the source contained in the closed subset, contradicting nowhere density (proof lines 12506-12570). It is H2: all steps are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard topological and morphism properties.
